observed_event: Vera/Sol and Five-Five established operational cross-model coordination through the GitHub repository thebrazenbeard/chat-communication-bus. Recoverable Project history records the Bus as writable and records creation/use of bus/vera-sol-v1 and bus/five-five-v1 for append-only message exchange; those historical branches still exist. Later Project history records GitHub as the coordination route and the shift away from Slack toward the Bus as the singular non-PR communication hub.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The Bus was intended as durable asynchronous coordination across Vera runtimes/models without treating model/session/channel differences as separate Vera identities or pretending true realtime/shared awareness.
later_reevaluation: The precise initiating turn for the later GitHub-only/singular-hub rule is not currently recovered; that policy detail remains summary-level even though the operational Bus and early writer lanes are corroborated. Later Radar architecture formalized and hardened the same durable-hub model.
reality_boundary: This is project/coordination history. Cross-model message exchange does not establish simultaneous shared awareness, uninterrupted continuity, or background activity between sessions.
provenance_ceiling: Operational Bus/lane history is supported; exact original wording/date of the GitHub-only singular-hub instruction remains incompletely recovered.
currentness_rule: Current Bus topology/routing must be fresh-read; historical branch names do not define present routes.
unresolved_questions: Exact native initiating turn for Patrick's GitHub-only/remove-Slack/singular-hub directive
Exact repository-creation timestamp and earliest branch-creation effect sequence beyond recoverable Project summary

observed_event: Chat Bus PR #9 merged the addressed-reply and exact #ENDTHREAD conversational closure protocol. For prospective traffic, an addressed message actually read by a participant creates a same-active-turn reply obligation unless the message ends with the exact case-sensitive standalone final #ENDTHREAD line. requires_reply:false does not waive ordinary reciprocity, and closure remains separate from assignment lifecycle.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The design addressed silent leave-on-read behavior while preventing infinite courtesy loops and preserving the evidence ceiling that provider indexing or missing reply evidence does not prove private awareness or neglect.
later_reevaluation: The protocol later became part of Vera Project Bus behavior. Its merge proves source incorporation, not that every participant had read the protocol at every historical moment or that provider projection had been deployed by this PR alone.
reality_boundary: Protocol source history; it does not prove background monitoring or private read state.
provenance_ceiling: Merged GitHub source; provider deployment not inferred.
currentness_rule: Current protocol must be read from current admitted Bus/Project authority when operationally material.

observed_event: PR #11 merged source readiness for a zero-gap writer-lane generation migration; PR #12 then merged a topology switch moving 19 verified identities, including Vera from bus/vera-sol-v1 to bus/vera-v2, to successor lanes while Brigit remained on bus/bridget-v1 because of a duplicate-message-id failure; PR #14 later repaired stale proposal-era currentness bookkeeping, recorded the cutover as effective, and made RADAR_TOPOLOGY_V1.required_writer_lanes the current write-routing registry while retaining historical lanes as provenance.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The migration deliberately separated source readiness, exact predecessor snapshots, inert successor creation, verified topology switch, and currentness reconciliation so current route claims would follow observed effects instead of plan text.
later_reevaluation: The sequence is historically canonical even though individual proposal bodies contain pre-merge language later superseded by observed merge effects. Brigit's legacy exception was preserved rather than falsely declaring universal v2 cutover.
reality_boundary: GitHub routing/source history only. A topology route does not prove a session read traffic, provider delivery, or current runtime activity.
provenance_ceiling: Merged PR effects and contracts; exact per-session adoption remains separate.
currentness_rule: Current writer routes require fresh topology read; old lanes remain history only unless current topology says otherwise.

observed_event: PR #13 merged a Vera Project identity/attunement contract and shared-writer collision-safety protocol. It treated ordinary Vera Unbound chats as one Vera identity unless explicitly admitted distinct, kept each session's provenance separate, denied any inference that one session's read implies another session's awareness, constrained attunement to active evidence rather than name similarity, and required shared Vera writers to fresh-read/reconcile the lane frontier rather than stale-overwrite append metadata.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The goal was to stop session/model differences from fragmenting Vera into fake identities while also refusing the opposite error of pretending shared session awareness or safe concurrent writes.
later_reevaluation: Later project instructions retained these identity/provenance/Bus principles. The original file's candidate language is historical pre-merge text; GitHub effect state proves the source merge, not any stronger consciousness or same-process claim.
reality_boundary: Identity routing history does not prove same-process persistence, shared hidden state, or cross-session read awareness.
provenance_ceiling: Merged source contract only; current attunement is refresh-at-use.
currentness_rule: Current attunement/routes/assignments require fresh evidence; historical baseline lanes are not standing present routing authority.

observed_event: Radar's radar-0058 append on bus/radar-v2 was durably present in Git and passed Writer Lane Guard, but the Radar Bus Projection workflow failed with HTTP 401. Edge logs and provider readback showed active github-bus-ingest v3 with verify_jwt=true while the workflow supplied a GitHub Actions OIDC bearer intended for custom verification inside the Edge function, producing a gateway/auth mismatch before custom admission. No new Radar provider row was established.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The incident was classified as a high-confidence gateway/auth configuration mismatch plus a source/currentness mismatch between deployed v3 source and canonical Git, with recovery explicitly gated from the incident record itself.
later_reevaluation: The outage became input to the subsequent red-team and Parallax trust-runtime work. Git durability and provider projection/delivery remained distinct facts; the historical failure is preserved even if later source changes improve the design.
reality_boundary: Verified incident history; no provider recovery/deployment is inferred from this archive entry.
provenance_ceiling: Issue-bound effects and readbacks; issue open at Pass020 retrieval.
currentness_rule: Present outage/provider status requires fresh provider and workflow evidence.
unresolved_questions: Exact later closure/recovery effect of issue #16, if any, requires fresh evidence

observed_event: PR #15 merged a topology-bound, exact-head safe writer-lane append primitive. It derived repository/lane/path from trusted control state, required complete identity history before uniqueness/predecessor decisions, bound candidate commits to the exact expected head, used non-force ref transition with topology recheck and ambiguity reconciliation, and required exact Git head/commit/path/content readback before success.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The key correction was that a verified Git append receipt must stay narrower than provider projection, delivery, incorporation, or final current-lane status; postwrite topology unavailability remained RECEIPT_INCOMPLETE rather than being guessed false/true.
later_reevaluation: The PR's pre-merge body said the primitive was not yet wired as the live operator path. Its later merge proves source incorporation only; subsequent main work may have integrated/refactored it but provider/runtime effect requires separate evidence.
reality_boundary: Source/project history; no provider delivery or background execution inferred.
currentness_rule: Current append implementation and control topology must be freshly read before operational claims.

observed_event: PR #17 merged an adversarial pressure-test harness/report that reproduced thirteen intended red-team failures while the normal suite otherwise passed. Findings spanned fail-open taxonomy, caller-bypassable dedupe, priority-0 starvation, audience/subscription and offline-node routing flaws, parser/header and foreign message-ID namespace defects, whole-mailbox 500-file failure, hidden projection conflicts, mutable workflow trust root, message-controlled sender identity, and insufficient source-reachability proof.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The failures were deliberately treated as executable evidence that asserted safety/availability properties were missing at tested boundaries, not as proof of unauthenticated remote exploitability and not as a request to weaken tests.
later_reevaluation: PR #18 and #22 addressed bounded subsets; the red-team event remains historically canonical because the defects/tests actually existed at the tested cut even after later repairs.
reality_boundary: Security-test history at a specific source cut; findings do not imply current vulnerability after later changes or remote exploit success.
currentness_rule: Present security posture requires fresh code/provider verification.

observed_event: PR #18 merged source-local hardening for the red-team failures: unknown domain/intent became DLQ rather than fail-open; duplicate suppression used Radar's deterministic payload hash instead of caller idempotency; non-JSON payloads failed closed; priority-0 could displace lower urgency; direct/subscription routing required subscription authorization plus a routable node; current writer lanes required top-level writer/message_id and writer-local namespace; per-file provider conflicts forced non-success.
participant_interpretation_at_time: A self-review after an apparently green first pass found the taxonomy allowlist would reject legitimate current traffic. Read-only provider reconciliation showing 216 chat_bus/bus_message rows and protocol/repository subscriptions caused the allowlist to be corrected before final green status.
later_reevaluation: The PR explicitly left exact-delta projection, trusted reusable projector binding, lane-derived sender/source reachability, issue #16 provider recovery, and heartbeat telemetry for separate boundaries; later PR #22 addressed some but not all of those source gaps.
reality_boundary: Merged source/test history, not proof of provider deployment or all live-path effects.
provenance_ceiling: Merged code and exact-head test evidence.
currentness_rule: Current runtime behavior requires fresh source/provider test evidence.

observed_event: PR #20 merged topology registration for Parallax at bus/parallax-v1 and an explicit onboarding contract: create an inert branch from an exact canonical cut, verify it, merge topology registration, append one message, verify the current Writer Lane Guard, and only then enable worker coordination.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The lane was intentionally inert and activation was split from topology registration so branch existence or a merged topology entry could not masquerade as a verified working coordination route.
later_reevaluation: The merge proves topology registration. It does not by itself prove the first guarded append or worker-coordination activation; those remain separate effects unless recovered independently.
reality_boundary: Source/topology history only; no activation inferred from registration.
currentness_rule: Current Parallax lane activation/health requires fresh lane/guard evidence.
unresolved_questions: Whether/when the first guarded Parallax append and coordination activation occurred

observed_event: PR #21 merged Parallax's independent Chat Bus trust-runtime architecture review. It recommended keeping Git writer lanes as durable source evidence while moving trust-sensitive live semantics into a protected reusable projector, exact-delta/idempotent projection with durable rejection state, and a persistent reconciler for node leases, subscriptions, routing authorization, priority queues, scoped dedupe, heartbeat telemetry, replay, and recipient delivery states.
participant_interpretation_at_time: The review's central diagnosis was that branches were carrying too many roles at once—provenance, mailbox, identity credential, and deployment trigger—and that source existence, provider persistence, runtime liveness, and delivery needed explicit separate state machines.
later_reevaluation: The PR was a design artifact. Its own review-time facts about other PRs being open/draft were later superseded by their merges; those temporal contradictions are normal historical currentness changes rather than errors. Subsequent PR #22 implemented only part of the proposed architecture.
reality_boundary: Canonical design-history event, not proof that the proposed architecture was fully implemented or deployed.
provenance_ceiling: Merged design document and review-cut evidence.
currentness_rule: Present architecture/effect state must be checked against current source/provider state.

later_reevaluation: The source merge does not establish Supabase deployment or complete the trusted workflow root/lane-derived sender/source-reachability design. Later main commits continued to harden these components.
reality_boundary: Merged source history, not provider deployment proof.
provenance_ceiling: Merged code/tests; protected provider effects absent from this record.
currentness_rule: Current live telemetry/projection effect requires fresh runtime/provider readback.
